<h1>HeartLuma privacy policy</h1>
<p class="notice"></p>
</header>

<section>
<h2>Who operates HeartLuma</h2>
<p>HeartLuma is being developed by Zaki Saud as an individual developer. This operator name must be confirmed against the developer’s legal and Apple Developer records before publication. No registered company is represented by this draft.</p>
</section>

<section>
<h2>Your account</h2>
<p>You provide an email address and password to create an account. Supabase Auth processes sign-up, email confirmation, sign-in and session management. Its authentication service stores account identifiers, email, password verification information and authentication records. Passwords are not shared with your partner.</p>
<p>Your device holds session credentials so you can stay signed in. HeartLuma encrypts the saved session with AES-GCM and protects its encryption key using the iOS Keychain. Authentication credentials are not sent to the Notes widget.</p>
</section>

<section>
<h2>Your partner connection</h2>
<p>HeartLuma stores your account’s membership in a couple, connection timestamps and invitation records. Invitation codes are random, expire and can be used once. The database stores a hash of the code. A code you copy or share is disclosed through the destination you choose; share it only with your intended partner.</p>
<p>Current members can access their own couple’s membership information. Other couples cannot access it through the normal application permissions. The app does not currently display a partner profile or partner email.</p>
</section>

<section>
<h2>Private notes</h2>
<p>HeartLuma stores the notes you send, their sender, intended recipient, couple, timestamps and a retry identifier. A note may contain sensitive information you choose to write. Notes are limited to 160 characters. The Home screen shows the latest authorized note received, but older notes remain in the database; displaying a newer note does not delete the older notes.</p>
<p>The application permits a recipient to read notes addressed to them while both people remain members of that couple. Sending a note does not give the sender a sent-history reading permission. Supabase and authorized operators may have privileged access needed to operate and protect the service. Notes are not end-to-end encrypted.</p>
<p>Unsent drafts and retry receipts stay in app memory, not persistent note storage. They are cleared when the account-scoped state is discarded, including logout or app restart. A recipient can independently copy, photograph or share a note; HeartLuma cannot erase those copies.</p>
</section>

<section>
<h2>The Notes widget</h2>
<p>The app may save a protected local display snapshot of your latest authorized received note for the iPhone Home Screen widget. The app and widget share this snapshot through an App Group. Widget control preferences contain a scope digest and state, not your authentication credentials.</p>
<p>The snapshot is limited by authorization expiry and freshness checks and is cleared or invalidated on logout or a detected account or membership change. The app must open and synchronize to learn remote changes. iOS controls refresh timing and can retain a rendered widget image; removal is not guaranteed to be immediate. People near an unlocked device may see its widget.</p>
</section>

<section>
<h2>Service providers and operational information</h2>
<p>Supabase provides authentication and database processing. Network services receive information needed to handle connections, such as IP addresses and request or security records. Email delivery providers process confirmation emails. Hosting location, provider settings, subprocessors and operational-log retention must be confirmed before this draft is published.</p>
<p>The reviewed app has no configured advertising, tracking or product-analytics SDK. Development builds use Expo development tooling. This statement is not a guarantee that infrastructure providers produce no operational records.</p>
<p>The privacy page is being prepared for free HTTPS hosting on GitHub Pages, without a custom domain. It has not been published. If this hosting is activated, GitHub will process visitor IP addresses for security purposes. The static policy page will not contain account sign-in, private notes or deletion forms.</p>
</section>

<section>
<h2>Retention and leaving HeartLuma</h2>
<p>Logging out clears or invalidates local account state and widget eligibility. It does not delete your remote account, partner connection or stored notes. A lost or offline device may retain data until it can process changes. Encrypted-session and device-backup behavior can differ after reinstall or device restoration.</p>
<p>There is currently no general in-app unpair or blocking operation. Solo-space recovery only moves a person who has no partner into a partner’s space. It is not account deletion.</p>
<p>Account deletion is being prepared and is not available in this development build. No deletion request can be submitted here. The proposed release process would verify your identity and explicitly confirm permanent deletion before a trusted server removes your Auth account, membership, invitations you created, and notes you sent or received. It would not delete your partner’s account. Notes exchanged with you, including notes your partner sent to you, would be removed from the active database. Non-content couple records may remain.</p>
<p>The deletion process, completion handling, retention schedule and any legally required exceptions must be approved, implemented and verified before publication or public release. Backups, security records, external copies and system-rendered widget images may remain for different periods. This draft promises neither instant nor permanent erasure of every copy.</p>
</section>

<section>
<h2>Security and your choices</h2>
<p>HeartLuma uses authenticated sessions and database access rules to limit access between couples. No system can guarantee complete security. Keep your password, email account, invitation codes and device secure, and avoid sharing information you do not want your partner to retain.</p>
<p>You can choose whether to send a note, share an invitation or place a widget on your Home Screen. A local widget snapshot is not a guarantee that only you can see the screen.</p>
</section>

<section>
<h2>Contact, privacy requests and updates</h2>
<p>The support email has not been finalized. No support address or contact link is available in this development build. A monitored contact channel must be established before public release. The privacy policy has not been published, so no public policy link is available yet.</p>
<p>Before release, the operator must establish a working channel for support, privacy, deletion and abuse concerns, define response and retention practices, and publish an effective date. Material changes will be described in the published policy and communicated where required. This draft has no effective date.</p>
</section>

<section>
<h2>Future HeartLuma Moments</h2>
<p>Photo sharing and the Moments widget are not implemented. This policy does not describe an operating photo service. Before Moments launches, the policy and privacy disclosures must be updated for photo selection, metadata removal, private storage, replacement/deletion, widget caching and content-safety handling.</p>
</section>

</main>
